image_transform: Whole views; aspect-preserving fit into common tiles, padding and identical labels. No flip or content crop.
cadence: All recorded frames retained; 10 control frames per playback second; display only.

notes.text: Maintain grasp; gently reduce the apparent pitch offset and move toward the slot center while staying above it.
Complete the small pitch correction and lower gradually; plug remains retained and nearly centered over the visible slot.
Approach straight downward with fixed orientation and a tiny lateral centering correction, watching the remaining gap.
Plug appears centered at the mouth; begin a shallow insertion with small vertical increments while keeping the grasp fixed.
Contact imprint shifted while the tip barely advanced. Relieve contact slightly and correct depth alignment toward the visible slot rather than continuing to push.
The depth correction tilted the retained plug against the mouth. Undo it gently to restore a vertical plug before advancing farther.
Pitch has returned close to the retained alignment. Apply a very small depth correction and a shallow downward seating motion.
The imprint is moving relative to the fingers while the plug remains at the rim. Relieve downward pressure and test a 1 mm depth alignment correction.
Positive depth motion tilted the plug at its constrained tip. Restore the previous depth alignment and test a very shallow seating motion.
The tactile pitch is again close to vertical after compensation. Advance 1 mm downward with a small visible lateral centering correction.
The plug appears stopped at the mouth while the tactile patch slides. Lift 3 mm to clear the rim before realigning; retain a slightly smaller opening.
Increase clearance slowly and command a smaller opening to limit the observed slip before another alignment attempt.
With a visible gap restored, adjust the depth position by about 1.5 mm at the plug and refine pitch before lowering again.
Lower 1.5 mm at the revised depth alignment, retaining the plug and monitoring contact.
The plug reached the mouth without visible imprint shift. Begin another shallow downward insertion at fixed alignment.
The contact patch shifted while the tip stayed at the rim. Raise 3 mm to remove the constraint before correcting the remaining pitch error.
With clearance restored, compensate the residual tactile pitch while approximately pivoting about the connector tip.
Lower the pitch-corrected connector toward the socket without further lateral motion, checking whether contact remains stable.
The plug has reached the socket mouth with little tactile change. Try a further 1 mm straight insertion, watching for relative slip rather than assuming seating.
The imprint moved relative to the hand again. Lift off the mouth, then test a 1 mm depth correction away from the camera while preserving the pitch alignment.
Approach and test the new depth alignment in small downward steps, monitoring whether the plug moves with the hand.
The plug still stops at the rim. Clear it vertically, then test the opposite depth side of the mouth without changing pitch.
Withdraw farther to obtain unambiguous clearance, restoring the previous yaw before reassessing the retained plug's pitch and depth.
With the plug fully clear, compensate its changed tactile pitch by rotating about the approximate tip, keeping the visible lateral alignment.
Refine pitch slightly and approach the socket from clear space, stopping above the mouth for another visual check.
The retained plug is visibly centered with a small gap. Lower 3 mm at fixed pitch and depth to reach the mouth.
The approach reached the mouth without an obvious tactile shift. Test a shallow 1 mm insertion while holding the current alignment.
Repeated rim stops suggest more than depth error. Clear the socket and correct the cross-sensor skew with a modest yaw adjustment, approximately preserving the tip center.
Finish the small yaw compensation while clear, then approach cautiously without changing depth or pitch.
The plug is at the mouth with little imprint change. Test a shallow straight insertion at the revised yaw alignment.
Continue a limited 2 mm seating test with fixed alignment and retained grasp; compare plug exposure and both contact patches before making further corrections.
The latest seating test caused clear relative slip and skew. Withdraw vertically by 10 mm for definite clearance before recalibrating the plug orientation.
With definite clearance, reduce residual pitch and shift the connector tip toward the camera-side depth of the slot; retain a visible approach gap.
Approach at the new depth alignment, correcting the small visible lateral offset and preserving the now-compensated pitch.
Close the remaining visible gap while making a small residual pitch correction about the tip; keep the depth and lateral tip location approximately fixed.
The plug reached the mouth without an obvious contact-patch shift. Continue a bounded 3 mm straight seating motion at the current alignment.
The plug is stopped and the opposing imprints are strongly skewed. Clear the rim and reduce the yaw correction while keeping the tip laterally centered.
While clear, compensate the opposing-pad depth asymmetry with positive yaw about the approximate tip. The yaw sign remains uncertain, so keep the plug above the mouth.
Approach the mouth at the revised yaw without further lateral motion, monitoring whether the contact imprint remains stable.
The plug followed the approach to the mouth. Test 1.5 mm of straight insertion and inspect for renewed relative slip.
The latest test again slipped at the rim. Withdraw 5 mm, then move 4 mm away from the camera to correct the estimated plug-versus-slot depth offset, keeping orientation fixed.
Lower toward the mouth at the revised depth, leaving the orientation unchanged so the effect of this alignment correction can be assessed.
At the mouth again with a stable imprint; test one millimeter of insertion at the adjusted depth before deciding on further alignment.
Rim contact still causes slip. Withdraw well clear and undo the large yaw adjustment, approximately preserving the tip position, to reassess the opposing contact skew.
With the plug clearly free, compensate the current tactile pitch and opposing-pad depth skew together, approximately pivoting about the tip.
Keep the corrected orientation and approach with a 4 mm camera-side depth adjustment, also centering the tip over the slot in the head view.
While still clear, compensate the remaining opposing-pad depth skew with a small yaw rotation, translating to approximately preserve the tip center.
The exposed plug leans left despite the pitch/yaw correction. Correct that roll while approximately pivoting at the tip and retaining clearance.
The exposed plug now appears more vertical and centered. Approach the mouth at fixed orientation, stopping short of a deep insertion.
The plug is just at the slot with the corrected roll. Test one millimeter of straight insertion and check whether the contact patches stay fixed.
The last shallow step left the tactile patches nearly unchanged. Continue a limited 2 mm straight seating motion, preserving alignment.
The last step caused clear slip. Withdraw 8 mm, then correct the accumulated camera-side depth offset by moving 7 mm away from the camera while keeping orientation fixed.
The plug is clearly above the slot after the depth correction. Approach 6 mm straight down without adding another orientation change.
Close the small remaining gap and test a shallow insertion at the new depth while maintaining the retained plug's orientation.
The plug again stops behind the visible mouth and slips. Clear the rim, then bring its depth 5.5 mm toward the camera without changing the compensated orientation.
The plug did not clearly follow the short withdrawal. Command full closure and lift gently to establish definite clearance before another insertion attempt.
With a visible gap, compensate a little more of the opposing-pad yaw skew, approximately pivoting at the tip and maintaining clearance.
Lower through the remaining visible gap with the current yaw and grasp held fixed, stopping at the mouth.
The plug reached the mouth with little patch displacement. Continue a bounded 2 mm seating motion at fixed alignment.
The mouth still blocks advancement. Clear it vertically, then correct the estimated camera-side depth error by moving 8 mm away from the camera, with orientation fixed.
With clear space restored, reduce the residual tactile pitch error while approximately pivoting at the plug tip; approach only partway to the mouth.
Close the visible gap with a 3 mm straight approach at the corrected depth and pitch, watching for the first sign of relative slip.
The plug stops behind the visible mouth. Clear it, restore camera-side depth by about 8 mm at the tip, and make small residual pitch/yaw corrections while clear.
Approach straight down through the remaining visible gap at the corrected depth, retaining the current orientation.
The plug reached the mouth without obvious contact-patch displacement. Test a further 1.5 mm straight seating motion.
The seating test still slips. Withdraw fully and return gradually to the native holding opening so the less-distorted tactile shape can guide a fresh alignment.
While clear, correct the visible sideways lean and remaining tactile pitch, approximately pivoting about the plug tip, then approach partway toward the mouth.
Refine the small remaining lean and center the tip over the visible opening while approaching 3 mm, preserving tip depth approximately.
The tip looks vertical and centered with a small gap. Lower 2.5 mm at fixed orientation and depth to reach the mouth.
Clear the mouth and reduce the accumulated yaw by about 0.2 rad, using the opposing tactile depth offset to reassess alignment and approximately preserving the tip center.
The reduced yaw exposes a slight rightward lean. Correct that roll about the approximate tip and approach 2 mm while keeping a visible clearance.
Refine the remaining small visible lean while preserving the tip center, and lower through the last few millimeters of clearance.
At the mouth with a nearly vertical plug and stable contact shape, test one millimeter of straight insertion.
Only a small contact displacement appeared in the last step. Limit the next seating test to another millimeter, with no lateral or angular change.
The latest millimeter clearly slipped at the rim. Lift clear and make a small 1.5 mm depth correction away from the camera, keeping the improved orientation unchanged.
Close the small restored gap and test the revised depth alignment with a limited 2 mm straight downward motion.
The plug followed most of the latest approach. Test another millimeter slowly at fixed alignment, watching for renewed sliding in the fingers.
The plug remains blocked despite near-level pitch. Clear the rim and test a larger depth correction away from the camera, keeping the improved orientation unchanged.
Approach 5 mm straight down at the revised depth, stopping near the socket mouth to inspect alignment.
The plug is centered with about a millimeter of visible clearance. Close that gap slowly without changing orientation or depth.
The shallow step slipped at the rim. Clear the tip and test a 2 mm camera-side depth correction, preserving the nearly level pitch and current yaw.
Approach the mouth at the revised depth with a 2.5 mm straight downward motion, checking whether the plug continues to follow the fingers.
Continue a bounded 2.5 mm seating attempt at the current centered, nearly level alignment, watching plug exposure and contact deformation.
The contact shape shows another rim stop. Withdraw and test a 6 mm depth correction away from the camera, retaining the current near-level orientation.
Approach through the restored gap at the revised depth, preserving the nearly level plug orientation and lateral centering.
The plug stopped visibly behind the slot and slid upward in the fingers. Lift clear and return 5.5 mm toward the camera, keeping the current near-level orientation.
Close the restored gap at this intermediate depth with a 3 mm straight approach; keep orientation and grasp unchanged to assess contact.
The plug again stopped at the mouth. Try a bounded 1 mm depth and 0.5 mm lateral centering adjustment with only a shallow downward advance.
The small depth probe tilted the contact patch instead of inserting. Lift 5 mm without further rotation to read the unconstrained plug alignment.
The free contact shape is level again. Approach with a 2 mm depth correction away from the camera while keeping the visible centering and orientation fixed.
Close the remaining small gap at this depth with a limited straight descent; inspect whether the plug continues to follow the hand.
The tip remains at the rim. Test a small camera-side depth sweep with very shallow downward motion, watching for a drop into the opening rather than pushing farther.
The depth sweep tilted the plug at its constrained tip. Relieve that tilt and make a small negative yaw adjustment before another shallow seating attempt.
The contact patch has returned to a level shape. Test one millimeter of straight insertion at the slightly reduced yaw.
The plug still slides at the rim. Clear it and test a 1.5 mm lateral correction toward the visible left side of the slot, leaving pitch and depth unchanged.
The plug now appears laterally centered over the opening. Close the visible gap with a 3 mm straight approach at unchanged depth and orientation.
The plug is stopped just above the mouth. Hold height and test a 2 mm camera-side depth sweep without adding downward pressure, looking for the opening.
The depth sweep pivots the plug at a constrained tip. Clear it, restore the level-depth position, and correct the small remaining sideways lean about the approximate tip.
Approach the mouth with the plug now level and laterally centered, preserving this alignment through a 3 mm descent.
Use a small depth/lateral centering adjustment and slight yaw refinement at the mouth, limiting further downward travel to half a millimeter.
Relieve the renewed contact skew, then refine depth 1.3 mm away from the camera and slightly reduce yaw while clear of the rim.
The free imprints are level and the plug is centered. Approach 3 mm straight down at this refined depth and yaw.
Search gently across the mouth toward the camera with only 0.5 mm downward travel, checking whether the constrained tip can enter rather than simply pivot.

The sweep produced a pivot rather than entry. Clear the mouth, restore the prior depth, and remove the residual hand roll indicated by matching opposing contact endpoints, approximately preserving the tip center.
With roll removed and clear space available, compensate the small remaining tactile pitch about the approximate tip while approaching partway to the mouth.
Approach through the visible gap with fixed pitch and yaw, making a small leftward centering correction toward the slot.
Relieve the rim contact briefly, correct the remaining visible rightward offset by 1 mm, and return slowly to the same approach height.
The tip is now laterally centered. Refine yaw by a small amount inferred from the opposing contact offset while testing less than a millimeter of insertion.
The plug still slips at the mouth. Clear the rim and sample a nearby depth 1.5 mm farther from the camera while retaining the current centered orientation.
Approach the visible gap slowly at the new depth, preserving the plug's centered orientation and grasp.
The plug followed the last descent with stable contact patches. Close the remaining millimeter slowly at fixed alignment.
The tip is still blocked despite good centering. Relieve contact briefly and make small pitch/yaw corrections inferred from the free tactile shape, approximately pivoting at the tip.
Test one millimeter of straight insertion after the small angular refinement; keep the grasp and lateral position fixed.
The plug is still stopped visibly behind the opening. Withdraw clearly, then bring it 8 mm toward the camera without changing the nearly level orientation.
Approach through the restored gap at the camera-side depth, with a small visible lateral centering correction and fixed orientation.
The plug followed the approach with stable contact patches. Close the remaining visible gap with a slow 2 mm straight descent.
The plug reached the mouth with no obvious patch displacement. Test one millimeter of straight insertion while retaining the current alignment.
The last millimeter slipped at the mouth. Relieve contact and correct the small residual pitch by 0.01 rad about the approximate tip, retaining depth and lateral alignment.
Lower through the restored small gap at the refined pitch, keeping the tip depth and lateral location fixed.
The plug followed the latest approach to the mouth with little contact movement. Test another millimeter of straight insertion at unchanged alignment.
